**CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ • The end of July and the start of August surprised many in the market: when US politicians finally agreed to extend the debt ceiling, all of the precious metals gave back some of their recent gains. However, surprisingly, gold continued to rise, eventually exceeding $1,700 on the 8th of August following the downgrade of US credit ratings by one agency. Palladium, platinum and silver all tried to push higher but suffered large downward spikes in their prices as global economic woes weighed on the outlook for industrial demand for each metal. In price terms, platinum strongly outperformed palladium but was in turn outperformed by gold as investors looked for safe haven assets. • On COMEX and NYMEX, investors increased their net long exposure to all four of the precious metals in the week to the 2nd of august. Gold positions increased to their longest for at least a decade and investors were duly rewarded as gold hit new highs. In contrast, many recent palladium investors will have been washed from the market by the steep decline in this metal’s price. • For the third consecutive week, ETF holdings increased for three of the precious metals (gold, silver and platinum) but fell for palladium. Gold and silver seemed to benefit from the worries over the health of almost every developed nation’s finances. Platinum saw continued buying interest but palladium saw further outflows showing dwindling investor interest or, perhaps, simple profit-taking. **David Jollie david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **08 August 2011** #### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 #### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 #### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 #### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 #### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **08 August 2011** ## **Gold CFTC data to 2 August 2011; ETF data to 5 August 2011.** ### **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

The price flickered higher on the 29th as US politicians seemed decreasingly likely to be able to agree on an extension to the debt ceiling there in time to meet their deadline. However, following the weekend, once an agreement had been reached in principle, gold fell back to the $1,615 level. News of more central bank buying provided some strength and disappointing US economic data raised the spectre of a doubledip recession, sending gold soaring to new highs of $1,670 on the 3rd of August. Central bank intervention in Switzerland and Japan saw the Dollar firm on the 4th, with gold plunging from $1,680 to a little over $1,640 later that day. It found support at this level and pushed higher before the US suffered a ratings downgrade on its debt after closing on the 5th: gold soared to a new high of $1,715 in Asian trading but has since given up some gains in retreating below $1,700. - Despite an agreement being made on extending the US debt ceiling, investors added to their net long speculative positioning in gold on COMEX in the week to the 2nd of August, boosting it by 1.3 million ounces to 33.1 million ounces, its highest level for at least ten years. Non-commercial long positions increased in number and options interest started to rebuild after the previous week’s options expiry. TOCOM investors added 184,000 ounces to their net long positions, increasing them to 585,000 ounces. Although the market is highly extended, the recent downgrading of the US debt ratings by one agency should see positioning increasing again this week. - ETF gold holdings increased by more than a million ounces for the second successive week and the third time in four weeks leading up to the 5th of August. Most funds recorded net inflows as record prices proved little deterrent to further purchasing. Total holdings now stand at a record 69 million ounces. ### **Gold Exchange Investment, April 09—August 11** 40 1,700 Gold price, $/oz

It peaked at $41.30 on the 27th but COMEX and ETF buying could not provide enough support to keep the price at that level. A weakening physical premium demonstrated the seasonal softness of industrial demand and, with the prospects of a breakthrough on US debt talks seemingly improving, silver slid back below $39.40 on the 1st of August. Agreement over an extension to the US debt ceiling and a strong gold price dragged silver to a high of $42 on the 4th but central bank intervention and margin calls driven by a weakening global economic outlook drove silver viciously lower that day to a low of below $39, an intraday fall of 7 per cent. Silver dropped further to $38 on the 5th before news of the USA downgrade generated enhanced safe haven buying: silver firmed to $40 in Asian trading on the 8th but has since retreated to $39.20. - While investors increased their long exposure to silver on COMEX in the week to the 2nd of August, the growth was less impressive than in the preceding four weeks, suggesting some lessening of bullish sentiment. Nonetheless, net long speculative positions did rise by 7.6 million ounces to 271 million ounces as investors

added to their long positions and covered some short contracts. If gold prices rise further, there is still sufficient room for silver speculators to add to their positions. - The week to the 5th of August saw net inflows of 4.4 million ounces into global silver ETFs. 23.1 million ounces have been purchased in the last four weeks with buying seen across most of the major funds, reflecting a clear turnaround in sentiment as the price has recovered. Total holdings now stand at 459 million ounces, up form their recent low of 436 million ounces. ### **Silver Exchange Investment, April 09—August 11** 450 50 Silver price, $/oz

- On the 26th of July, platinum firmed on the news that gold workers were to strike within South Africa. This reinforced the perception that strikes were increasingly likely in the platinum sector driving the price from an opening $1,790 to a high of $1,817 on the 27th before weakening. Weak US employment data and continued concerns over slowing Chinese growth pushed platinum slowly down towards $1,780 at the end of July. On the 1st, the proposed agreement on extending the US debt energised the platinum market briefly and saw platinum test $1,800 once again on the 1st and the 3rd. However, intervention in the foreign exchange markets drove liquidation of platinum on TOCOM, sending platinum lower. Perceptions of weak global economic demand and a strengthening Dollar drove platinum down to below $1,700 on the 5th, a fall of $100 in only two days! Stronger SGE purchasing has provided some strength since then, helping platinum back to $1,720. - In the week to the 2nd of August, net long speculative positioning in platinum increased by 97,000 ounces to 1.35 million ounces on NYMEX. This was the third successive weekly increase and helped platinum to crest the $1,800 mark in recovering from $1,720 or thereabouts, with exposure rising by 410,000 ounces in this period. Both larger and smaller speculators added to the number of long contracts they held. TOCOM investors were buyers too, boosting their net long position by 40,000 ounces to 550,000 ounces during the week. Given the sharp fall in the price since that point, we would expect to have seen long liquidation on NYMEX and on TOCOM. - Platinum ETF holdings increased for the third successive week, rising by 18,500 ounces to a total of 1.53 million ounces. Holdings have climbed by 59,000 ounces in three weeks and 273,000 ounces so far this year compared to last year’s total of 580,000 ounces. 4 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **08 August 2011** ## **Palladium CFTC data to 2 August 2011; ETF data to 5 August 2011.** # **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Palladium Investment (oz)** |**Date**|**Nymex**

On the 26th, the price spiked from $810 to $840 with unconfirmed rumours of short covering providing one possible explanation. Palladium retreated a little to $830 but found support there until With investors adding to their futures positions, the price challenged $840 on the 1st, rising to a short-lived high of $848 that day before falling back to the $830 support. With weak economic data emerging ever more regularly from the USA, stock markets started to tumble and margin calls sent palladium lower. It closed in on $800 on the 3rd but found only minimal levels of support, falling below this level later that day and eventually lurching to a $725 on the 5th following central bank intervention in the currency markets in Japan and Switzerland. • Net long speculative positions in palladium on NYMEX increased by 61,000 ounces or 3.2 per cent in the week to the 2nd of August after climbing by 13 per cent in the previous week. They now stand at 1.89 million ounces, just shy of the November 2010 record of 1.96 million ounces. Any attempts by investors to make new highs for the year were foiled by economic concerns which drove the price lower. Given the decrease in open interest since that date, we expect the next commitment of traders report to show a sharp decrease in net long positioning. • The week to the 5th of August again saw selling from the palladium ETFs with American investors the culprit on this occasion. This is the third successive week in which there has been net selling, in contrast to platinum which has seen fresh investor inflows. For the year to date, there has been net selling of 45,000 ounces of palladium across all the Exchange Traded Funds, a far cry from 2010 when investors took almost one million ounces of palladium off the market. 5 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** ### **Disclaimer:** This briefing is for our clients’ information purpose only.
